direct_answer: Lymphoedema is long-term swelling caused by a problem with the lymphatic system. It can make limbs heavy and movement harder alongside arthritis. Skin care, gentle movement, compression and specialist lymphoedema services can help. Infection (cellulitis) needs prompt treatment.

content:
Swelling in the legs or arms has many causes. Lymphoedema is one, and it can add to stiffness and fatigue when you also have arthritis.

This guide explains lymphoedema and practical self-care. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

What lymphoedema is

The lymphatic system drains fluid from tissues. When it does not work properly, fluid builds up and causes swelling. It can follow cancer treatment, infection, injury, or reduced mobility.

Self-care

  • Keep skin clean and moisturised.
  • Protect skin from cuts and insect bites.
  • Move gently and regularly.
  • Raise the limb when resting, if comfortable.
  • Wear compression garments if prescribed.

Specialist help

Your GP can refer you to a lymphoedema service. They can advise on compression, massage techniques and exercises.

If hands make compression hard

Ask about aids, wraps with Velcro, or help from a carer or nurse.

When to get help

  • Call 999 if you have chest pain or sudden breathlessness.
  • Get urgent help from NHS 111 or your GP if a limb becomes red, hot and painful or you feel unwell with a fever, as this can be cellulitis.
  • Get urgent advice for sudden swelling in one leg, which can be a blood clot.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Is all swelling lymphoedema?

No. Swelling has many causes, so see your GP.

Can exercise help?

Gentle movement helps lymph flow.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: Lymphoedema
  • NHS: Osteoarthritis
